A custom Palm Beach County Window & Door Schedule — Palm Beach County doesn't publish a fillable grid like Broward's BORA sheet, so this is built as its own clean document instead of a forced copy, using Florida Product Approval (FL#) numbers rather than Miami-Dade NOAs. Same engineering fields as Broward, plus Location and Egress.

Design pressures use the Broward County Fenestration Voluntary Wind Load Chart, FBC 8th Edition (2023) / ASCE 7-22, Wind 170 mph, Exposure C, buildings ≤ 30 ft — confirmed for use on Palm Beach County submittals too.

Matches Indian River County / City of Vero Beach's official Window and Door Application & Schedule (Rev. 4/2/2025) — same columns, same Component & Cladding pressure chart for One and Two-Family Dwellings. Set Wind Speed, Exposure, and Story below, then Auto-Calc.

Component and Cladding Worst Case Design Pressure chart, FBC 8th Edition, one/two-family dwellings with mean roof height ≤ 30 ft, Exposures B/C/D. 160 mph zone extends from CR 512 & 507 to the ocean per the current IRC Wind Speed Map — confirm which speed applies to this job site. End-Zone 5 is never less than 4 ft.

*Indicate Type of Window: (SH) Single Hung, (DH) Double Hung, (CAS) Casement, (HR) Horizontal Roller, (SLDR) Slider, or applicable window/door type. Zone 5 is never less than 4 ft from the end wall; Zone 4 is any intermediate location more than 4 ft from end walls. Net clear opening is the actual free/clear space when the window is open — not the rough opening — the actual opening a person can crawl through.

Miami Window & Door Schedule — same format as the Broward schedule. Every window/door opening from the Floor Plan tab is listed below; fill in the engineering fields per opening, then export. "Required Design Pressure" can be auto-filled from the Miami-Dade Wind Load Chart using the Mean Roof Height set on the Floor Plan tab.

Design pressures are pulled from the Miami-Dade County Wind Load Chart for Openings, based on ASCE 7-22, one/two-family dwellings and townhouses, mean roof height ≤ 30 ft, 175 mph (3-sec gust), Exposure C, Kd = 0.85, ASD. Effective wind area uses the rough opening (width × height), per standard practice. Always confirm against your current printed chart before submittal.

Project & Site Parameters

Fill in Wind Speed, Exposure and Mean Roof Height for this site, then pick a Pressure Calculation Method below. This is a pre-engineering estimate only — a Florida-licensed engineer must review, certify and seal it before permit submission.

Prefilled from the Window & Door Schedule; edit freely for a site-specific estimate.
C fits most of coastal South Florida (open terrain). Use B for a suburban/wooded lot, D only right on open water.
Height from the ground to the roof's midpoint. Match the Project Info bar above if you're not sure.
Almost every finished home or condo is "Enclosed." Use "Partially Enclosed" only if a large opening (garage door, broken window) will stay uncovered in the storm.
